dublinCore.title: Euler's Formula Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Euler's formula
Complex exponentials
Unit circle
Sine and cosine
Phasors
dublinCore.description: Interactive visualization of Euler's formula e^(i theta) = cos(theta) + i sin(theta): a vector rotating on the unit circle in the complex plane, synchronized with the cosine and sine traces of its real and imaginary parts.

learningObjectives: Explain how the rotating green vector on the unit circle represents e^(iθ), with its real-axis projection tracing cos(θ) and its imaginary-axis projection tracing sin(θ)
Predict the values of cos(θ) and sin(θ) at θ = 0, π/2, π and 3π/2, then confirm them with the angle slider and the read-out box
Explain why the sine and cosine traces are identical curves offset by a quarter turn, given that they are projections of the same rotating vector onto perpendicular axes
Trace how advancing θ through a full 2π rotation generates exactly one complete cycle of each wave
Evaluate Euler's identity by setting θ = π and confirming that e^(iπ) = −1
prerequisites: Complex numbers and the complex plane

misconceptions.misconception: Sine and cosine are two separate, unrelated waves
misconceptions.correction: They are the imaginary and real projections of one rotating unit vector, so they are driven by the same angle and differ only by a quarter-turn offset
misconceptions.evidence: Press Play and watch the red and blue dots move together; at θ = 0 cosine is at its maximum while sine is 0, and at θ = π/2 sine is at its maximum while cosine is 0

misconceptions.misconception: The vector gets longer or shorter as it rotates
misconceptions.correction: The length |e^(iθ)| is always 1 because cos²(θ) + sin²(θ) = 1; only the direction changes
misconceptions.evidence: At 0.25π both projections read 0.7071 and at 0.00π they read 1 and 0, but the tip stays on the unit circle

accessibility.screenReaderScript: Visualization of Euler's formula. A green unit vector rotates around the unit circle in the complex plane. Its real part traces a cosine wave and its imaginary part traces a sine wave. Play and Reset buttons, an angle slider from 0 to 2 pi and a speed slider from 0.1 to 5 control the rotation. A read-out box gives the angle in radians and degrees, the cosine, the sine and the complex number e to the i theta.

controls.label: Play / Pause
controls.description: Starts or stops the automatic rotation of the vector; the label switches between Play and Pause

controls.label: Reset
controls.description: Returns the angle to 0, clears the traces and pauses the animation

controls.label: Angle (π)
controls.description: Sets the angle θ in units of π from 0 to 2 (0 to 2π radians); moving it while the animation runs pauses the animation

controls.label: Speed
controls.description: Sets the rotation speed as a multiple of 1.2 rad/s

visualElements.description: Unit circle in the complex plane with the rotating green vector, blue real-axis projection, red imaginary-axis projection, dashed projection lines and an angle arc
Stacked cosine (blue) and sine (red) plots against θ from 0 to 2π with a faint full period, a bold swept trace, the current point and a dashed level line
Read-out box with θ in radians and degrees, cos(θ), sin(θ) and e^(iθ) in rectangular form

model.description: Advances θ at 1.2 rad/s times the speed setting and evaluates the tip e^(iθ) = (cos θ, sin θ) on the unit circle, plotting each coordinate against θ over one period

instructionalStrategies: Predict the projections before moving the angle slider
Special-angle exploration at multiples of π/4
extensions: Add the negative-frequency vector e^(−iθ) and show that the two add to 2cos(θ)
Show two phasors with different speeds and their sum
